scope: Bounded validation driver for synthetic supplied graphs, supporting independent_tiny_oracle.run_exhaustive and run_seeded fixture generation; no images, detector, production integration, or performance claim

input_transport.arguments: Exactly one fixture input file path is required; no stdin and no delegated process
input_transport.mode: Binary, seekable file; initial size checked before processing, byte budget also enforced while reading
input_transport.encoding: ASCII only; NUL, non-ASCII bytes and non-whitespace control characters are rejected
input_transport.record_separator: LF byte; final nonempty record may omit LF
input_transport.empty_file: Legal zero-request batch, no stdout records, exit 0
input_transport.line_byte_accounting: 65536 bytes maximum excluding LF, including every other byte such as optional CR
input_transport.file_byte_accounting: 67108864 bytes maximum, including every LF and CR
input_transport.record_count: At most 100000 records; the 100001st bounded line is rejected before parsing or solving

input_grammar.request: Q1 request_id template_chain_id template_closed n scene_count (sample_id positive_weight)*n (scene_chain_id scene_closed m e (pixel_id)*m (edge_sample_id edge_pixel_id)*e)*scene_count
input_grammar.unsigned_integer: One to 20 ASCII decimal digits; leading zeros allowed; no sign, exponent, decimal point, or embedded whitespace; pre-multiply/add checked against 18446744073709551615
input_grammar.ids: request_id, template_chain_id, sample_id, scene_chain_id, pixel_id and both edge IDs use the unsigned_integer domain
input_grammar.closed_flags: Exactly one token 0 or 1; 00, 01, signs and other values are invalid
input_grammar.positive_weight: One to 512 ASCII decimal digits, leading zeros allowed, mathematical value strictly positive; signs, exponent, decimal point and nondigits rejected before GMP construction
input_grammar.counts: n, scene_count, m and e are bounded unsigned integers validated before graph reserve/allocation/loops
input_grammar.extra_tokens: Fatal EXTRA_TOKEN, even if a complete valid request precedes them on the same line
input_grammar.topology: Template sample order and each scene pixel order are preserved exactly, not sorted by numeric IDs
input_grammar.request_ids: May repeat across records; a caller requiring unique request association must enforce its own uniqueness

validation_driver_limits_only.edge_capacity_rule: e <= n*m checked before edge allocation; counts are already <=8 so multiplication is bounded
validation_driver_limits_only.native_core_boundary: These are fixture-driver limits only. The native core remains arbitrary precision and is not restricted to tiny graphs by this protocol. External process wall/RSS/output guards remain required.

graph_validation_before_solve: Template physical sample IDs unique; exactly one positive weight is parsed per sample
Scene chain IDs unique, including unused/empty chains
Physical pixel IDs unique inside each scene chain, including closed repeated endpoints and unused chains
Compatibility edges unique inside each scene chain
Every edge endpoint refers to a parsed template sample and a parsed pixel of that scene chain
Every scene is parsed and validated before solve; no empty/no-edge shortcut skips validation
The same scene pixel may occur in distinct scene chains; distinct requests never reserve scene pixels

output_grammar.result: R1 request_id template_chain_id numerator independent_numerator total_weight has_case (scene_chain_id direction template_cut scene_cut if has_case=1) witness_count (sample_id pixel_id)*witness_count case_count edge_states fenwick_queries fenwick_updates fenwick_query_visits fenwick_update_visits maximum_integer_bits
output_grammar.numerics: Canonical base-10 exact integers; no floats; has_case is exactly 0 or 1; direction is signed 1 or -1 for legal results
output_grammar.absent_case: has_case=0 consumes no four case fields
output_grammar.witness: Original edge IDs in selected transformed-template order, exactly as returned by native core
output_grammar.framing: Each complete response ends in LF and is flushed; stdout contains only R1/E1 protocol records; Windows stdout is binary
output_grammar.allocation_and_budget: Each response is assembled with bounded append checks, then checked against the remaining cumulative stdout budget before writing. Budget rejection emits no partial R1. Operating-system I/O failure can physically truncate a write and is an exit-2 failure.
output_grammar.error_request_id: Most errors after parsing request_id use its normalized uint64 value; before that, for line/total/request-limit errors, or for malformed request_id, the fallback is 0
output_grammar.error_budget: E1 is emitted only if it also fits remaining stdout budget and stdout is usable. Otherwise no new complete stdout record is emitted, a fixed bounded stderr diagnostic is attempted, and the nonzero exit remains fatal.

fatal_error_codes_exit_1.INPUT_LIMIT: Initial fixture size or consumed logical input bytes exceed 64MiB
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.INPUT_CHARACTER: NUL, non-ASCII or illegal control byte
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.LINE_LIMIT: A record exceeds 65536 bytes before LF
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.EXTRA_TOKEN: Tokens remain after the complete counted request
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.INTEGER_TOKEN_LIMIT: Unsigned integer token is empty or longer than 20 bytes
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.UNSIGNED_DECIMAL: Unsigned integer token contains a nondigit, including a minus/plus sign
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.UNSIGNED_OVERFLOW: Unsigned decimal value exceeds uint64 max
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.COUNT_LIMIT: n, m, scene_count or e exceeds its per-field cap
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.BOOLEAN_TOKEN: closed flag token is not exactly 0 or 1
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.WEIGHT_TOKEN_LIMIT: Weight token is empty or longer than 512 bytes
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.WEIGHT_DECIMAL: Weight token contains a nondigit, including a minus/plus sign
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.WEIGHT_NOT_POSITIVE: Weight decimal token has value zero
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.DUPLICATE_PIXEL: Duplicate physical pixel inside one scene chain
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.UNKNOWN_EDGE_ENDPOINT: Edge endpoint is not in that template/scene chain
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.DUPLICATE_EDGE: Repeated compatibility edge in one scene chain
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.RESPONSE_LIMIT: One serialized response cannot fit 8192 bytes or a result exceeds serialization bounds
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.OUTPUT_LIMIT: Next full response cannot fit cumulative 64MiB stdout budget

fatal_failures_exit_2.CLI: Wrong argument count: bounded usage on stderr, no E1
fatal_failures_exit_2.BINARY_STDOUT: Windows binary stdout setup failed: bounded stderr, no E1
fatal_failures_exit_2.SOLVER_INVALID_GRAPH: Core rejected a graph independently accepted by the parser

termination: First fatal record stops the process; earlier complete R1 records remain, no later records are solved. Exit0 requires complete EOF with every request answered. Callers must require exit0 and exactly one matching R1 per fixture request for a successful audit.
malformed_test_guidance: For generic malformed-input checks require exit1, final complete E1 with a listed exit1 code, no R1 for the invalid request, and no later responses. If several defects coexist, do not require a particular code. Input/output cap and I/O cases may have no E1 if the error record cannot be emitted within the output budget. For precise code tests use one isolated defect.
execution_claim: Protocol/source prepared without compiling or executing the batch driver; acceptance requires parent-controlled bounded build and fixture audit. No interactive or native performance conclusion follows.
